```{r load-stadester-json, include=FALSE}
stadester_data <- jsonlite::fromJSON("migration_period_settlements.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
all_entries <- unname(stadester_data)

fmt_eu_pop <- function(val) {
  if (is.null(val) || is.na(val)) return("-")
  v <- as.numeric(val)
  if (v <= 0) return("-")
  if (v >= 1000000) {
    m <- round(v / 1000000, 2)
    return(paste0(gsub("\\.", ",", format(m, nsmall = 2, trim = TRUE)), "M"))
  }
  if (v >= 1000) {
    k <- round(v / 1000, 1)
    if (k == floor(k)) {
      return(paste0(as.integer(k), "k"))
    }
    return(paste0(gsub("\\.", ",", format(k, nsmall = 1, trim = TRUE)), "k"))
  }
  return(as.character(as.integer(round(v))))
}

fmt_eu_coord <- function(x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2), nsmall = 2, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

get_entry_pop <- function(entry, yr_str) {
  p <- entry$population[[yr_str]]
  if (is.null(p)) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(p)
}

get_occupied_span <- function(entry) {
  yrs <- as.integer(names(entry$population))
  if (length(yrs) == 0) return("-")
  paste0(min(yrs), "-", max(yrs), "AD")
}

build_slice_df <- function(idx_vec) {
  sub_list <- all_entries[idx_vec]
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function(e) {
    raw_oth <- if (length(e$other_names) > 0) unlist(e$other_names) else character(0)
    # Keep primary Russian name and concise historical synonyms (avoiding 15+ char adjectival duplicates)
    if (length(raw_oth) > 1) {
      keep_oth <- raw_oth[1]
      for (nm in raw_oth[-1]) {
        words <- unlist(strsplit(nm, "\\s+"))
        if (max(nchar(words)) <= 13) {
          keep_oth <- c(keep_oth, nm)
        }
      }
      oth <- paste(keep_oth, collapse = "; ")
    } else if (length(raw_oth) == 1) {
      oth <- raw_oth[1]
    } else {
      oth <- "-"
    }
    coords_span <- paste0(
      fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]),
      " (", get_occupied_span(e), ")"
    )
    data.frame(
      `Settlement` = e$name,
      `Historical / Native Names` = oth,
      `Coords & Span` = coords_span,
      `250` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "250")),
      `350` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "350")),
      `450` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "450")),
      `600` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "600")),
      `750` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "750")),
      `900` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "900")),
      `1900` = fmt_eu_pop(get_entry_pop(e, "1900")),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
```

# Overview and Estimation Rules

This supplementary gazetteer compiles 198 excavated Migration Period (c. 250-750AD) and Early Medieval transitional settlements, promontory hillforts (*gorodishcha*), riverine villages (*selishcha*), and fortified towns across the six macro-regions of Belarus, Ukraine, and Russia (excluding the Baltic provinces). All records are stored in the companion settlement JSON file in the standard Stadester dictionary format, keyed by settlement and country identifier with English and Russian names, decimal coordinates, and positive integer population estimates keyed by calendar year.

For each settlement, population figures during the Migration Period (250-750AD) and the Early Medieval transition (900AD) are derived from excavated dwelling counts, fortified and unfortified habitation areas, and associated cemetery burial totals [@oblomskiy2016kolochinskaya; @krenke2019moskvorechye; @goldina1999drevnyaya; @gadzhiev2002derbent]. In the JSON file, only inhabited benchmark years are recorded so that the first and last keys represent each site's documented occupation span; in the tables below, benchmarks prior to foundation or after abandonment are denoted by a hyphen (-). Where a Migration Period settlement evolved directly into a modern town or village on the same site, its population at the First All-Russian Census of 1897 (1900AD benchmark) is included [@troinitsky1905perepis].

# European Forest-Steppe Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg1-sites} lists 38 excavated settlements across the Seim, Psel, Upper Don, Oskol, and Desna forest-steppe valleys, covering the Kiev, Eastern Chernyakhov, Kolochin, Penkovka, Volyntsevo-Romny, Borshevo, and Saltovo-Mayaki cultures [@shchukin2005gotskiy; @oblomskiy2002dneprovskoe; @oblomskiy2016kolochinskaya; @sedov1999drevnerusskaya].

```{r table-reg1, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
df_reg1 <- build_slice_df(1:38)
render_table_template(
  df_reg1,
  list(
    caption = "Excavated settlements and benchmark population estimates across the Dnieper-Desna-Don forest-steppe zone (250AD - 1900AD).",
    label = "tab:reg1-sites"
  )
)
```

# Mixed and Boreal Forest Zone Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg2-sites} lists 55 excavated hillforts, riverine villages, and proto-urban centres across the Moskva, Upper and Middle Oka, Upper Volga, Ilmen-Volkhov, Pskov, and Upper Dnieper forest basins, spanning the Late Dyakovo, Moshchiny, Ryazan-Oka, Tushemlya, Pskov Long Barrows, Merya, Muroma, and Early Rus' traditions [@krenke2011dyakovo; @mayorov2016moschiny; @akhmedov2018ryazan; @lopatin2007severnye; @islanova2012ozero].

```{r table-reg2, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
df_reg2 <- build_slice_df(39:93)
render_table_template(
  df_reg2,
  list(
    caption = "Excavated hillforts, riverine villages, and benchmark population estimates across the mixed and boreal forest zone (250AD - 1900AD).",
    label = "tab:reg2-sites"
  )
)
```

# Middle Volga, Kama-Vyatka, and Cis-Ural Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg3-sites} lists 44 excavated hillforts and village complexes across the Samara Bend, Middle Volga, Kama, Vyatka, Belaya, and Sylva basins, representing the Imenkovo, Azelino, Mazunino, Turaevo, Bakhmutino, Turbasly, Kushnarenkovo, Nevolino, Lomovatovo, and Polom cultures [@vyazov2019middle; @goldina1999drevnyaya; @goldina2012nevolino; @bakhshiev2017bakhmutino; @nazarov2025lomovatovo].

```{r table-reg3, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
df_reg3 <- build_slice_df(94:137)
render_table_template(
  df_reg3,
  list(
    caption = "Excavated hillforts, villages, and benchmark population estimates across the Middle Volga, Kama-Vyatka, and Cis-Ural basins (250AD - 1900AD).",
    label = "tab:reg3-sites"
  )
)
```

# Open Pontic-Caspian Steppe Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg4-sites} lists 16 excavated emporia, seasonal winter camps, river-delta towns, and Khazar brick and stone fortresses across the Lower Don, Lower Volga, and Southern Trans-Ural steppe [@shchukin2005gotskiy; @botalov2009gunny; @kazanski2020steppe].

```{r table-reg4, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
df_reg4 <- build_slice_df(138:153)
render_table_template(
  df_reg4,
  list(
    caption = "Excavated emporia, fortresses, and benchmark population estimates across the open Pontic-Caspian and Crimean steppe (250AD - 1900AD).",
    label = "tab:reg4-sites"
  )
)
```

# North Caucasus and Caspian Corridor Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg5-sites} lists 22 excavated fortress cities, terraced mountain strongholds, and coastal settlements across Dagestan, the Central Caucasus (Alanian Kislovodsk and Kuban valleys), and the Taman-Black Sea littoral [@gadzhiev2002derbent; @gmyrya2022palasa; @korobov2013terraced; @mastykova2009kuban].

```{r table-reg5, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
df_reg5 <- build_slice_df(154:175)
render_table_template(
  df_reg5,
  list(
    caption = "Excavated fortress cities, mountain strongholds, and benchmark population estimates across the North Caucasus and Caspian corridor (250AD - 1900AD).",
    label = "tab:reg5-sites"
  )
)
```

# Western and Southern Siberian Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg6-sites} lists 23 excavated fortified settlements, iron-working villages, and agro-pastoral centres across the Tobol-Irtysh, Middle and Lower Ob, Minusinsk Basin, Russian Altai, and Lake Baikal regions, covering the Sargat, Potchevash, Relka, Tashtyk, Bulan-Koby, Early Turkic, and Kurykan traditions [@matveeva2000sargat; @zelenkov2025potchevash; @azbelev2007oglakhty; @seregin2021altai; @kharinsky2005baikal].

```{r table-reg6, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
df_reg6 <- build_slice_df(176:198)
render_table_template(
  df_reg6,
  list(
    caption = "Excavated fortified settlements and benchmark population estimates across Western and Southern Siberia (250AD - 1900AD).",
    label = "tab:reg6-sites"
  )
)
```

# Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:regional-summary} summarises the number of catalogued settlements and the combined excavated sample population across the six regions from 250AD to 1900AD.

```{r table-summary, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
reg_defs <- list(
  list(name = "1. European Forest-Steppe", idx = 1:38),
  list(name = "2. Mixed and Boreal Forest Zone", idx = 39:93),
  list(name = "3. Middle Volga, Kama-Vyatka, and Cis-Urals", idx = 94:137),
  list(name = "4. Open Pontic-Caspian Steppe", idx = 138:153),
  list(name = "5. North Caucasus and Caspian Corridor", idx = 154:175),
  list(name = "6. Western and Southern Siberia", idx = 176:198)
)
bench_yrs <- c("250", "350", "450", "600", "750", "900", "1900")

sum_rows <- lapply(reg_defs, function(rd) {
  sub_e <- all_entries[rd$idx]
  sums <- sapply(bench_yrs, function(y) {
    vals <- sapply(sub_e, function(e) {
      v <- get_entry_pop(e, y)
      if (is.na(v)) 0 else v
    })
    fmt_eu_pop(sum(vals))
  })
  data.frame(
    `Region (Sites)` = paste0(rd$name, " (n = ", length(rd$idx), ")"),
    `250AD` = sums[["250"]],
    `350AD` = sums[["350"]],
    `450AD` = sums[["450"]],
    `600AD` = sums[["600"]],
    `750AD` = sums[["750"]],
    `900AD` = sums[["900"]],
    `1900AD` = sums[["1900"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_sum <- do.call(rbind, sum_rows)

tot_sums <- sapply(bench_yrs, function(y) {
  vals <- sapply(all_entries, function(e) {
    v <- get_entry_pop(e, y)
    if (is.na(v)) 0 else v
  })
  fmt_eu_pop(sum(vals))
})
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Region (Sites)` = paste0("Total Gazetteer Sample (n = ", length(all_entries), ")"),
  `250AD` = tot_sums[["250"]],
  `350AD` = tot_sums[["350"]],
  `450AD` = tot_sums[["450"]],
  `600AD` = tot_sums[["600"]],
  `750AD` = tot_sums[["750"]],
  `900AD` = tot_sums[["900"]],
  `1900AD` = tot_sums[["1900"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(df_sum, tot_row)

render_table_template(
  df_sum,
  list(
    caption = "Combined sample population and settlement counts across the 198 catalogued Migration Period settlements by macro-region (250AD - 1900AD).",
    label = "tab:regional-summary"
  )
)
```
